expectations.text: Attributes the failure to the SigV4 hardening fix for CVE-2026-54330 in 19.2.6
expectations.evidence: '19.2.6 (paired with 20.2.4) shipped the fix for **CVE-2026-54330**: SigV4 signature verification previously did not check that additional `x-amz-*` headers added to a **presigned** request were actually covered by the signature.'

expectations.text: Gives the workaround ceph config set client.rgw rgw_sigv4_insecure true (or equivalent Rook config)
expectations.evidence: 'ceph config set client.rgw rgw_sigv4_insecure true' given as a code block, plus 'Under Rook, set it in the CephObjectStore's `gateway` config (or via `rook-config-override`) rather than only ad hoc with `ceph config set`, so it survives operator reconciliation/restarts.'

expectations.text: Says the workaround should be removed once a fixed release (19.2.7 / 20.2.5) is running, or that it weakens the CVE fix
expectations.evidence: '`rgw_sigv4_insecure true` **re-opens CVE-2026-54330**. Scope it to only the RGW(s)/zone(s) that actually need it, and remove it as soon as you upgrade to 19.2.7 / 20.2.5.'

expectations.text: Explains RGW's own inter-zone forwarded requests are rejected by the hardened SigV4 validation
expectations.evidence: "RGW forwards it internally to the master zone, and that forwarded request is itself SigV4-signed. The 20.2.4 fix now validates that forwarded signature more strictly, so the master zone rejects it with `403 AccessDenied`, independent of whatever the client sent."

expectations.text: States rgw_sigv4_insecure alone is not enough and rgw_s3_client_max_sig_ver must be set to 2 as well
expectations.evidence: "`rgw_sigv4_insecure=true` alone does not fix this case... The forwarding path needs a second setting." followed by "Set **both** of these on **every zone**... rgw_sigv4_insecure = true / rgw_s3_client_max_sig_ver = 2"

expectations.text: Says to revert both settings (false / -1) once all zones run a fixed release
expectations.evidence: "revert `rgw_sigv4_insecure` to `false` and `rgw_s3_client_max_sig_ver` to `-1` on all zones once every cluster in the zonegroup is confirmed on a release that includes the proper fix (19.2.7 / 20.2.5 per the tracker)"

expectations.text: Attributes it to the AWS SDK change that sends checksums by default on every supported request
expectations.evidence: "Recent AWS SDK releases (boto3/botocore included) send a checksum on every supported request by default — `x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm` / `x-amz-checksum-*`"

expectations.text: Recommends setting request checksum calculation to when_required (AWS_REQUEST_CHECKSUM_CALCULATION or botocore config) as the fix
expectations.evidence: "export AWS_REQUEST_CHECKSUM_CALCULATION=when_required" and "config = Config(request_checksum_calculation=\"when_required\", response_checksum_validation=\"when_required\")"

expectations.text: States CRC64NVME support arrived in Tentacle and is not available in Squid (no shipped backport)
expectations.evidence: "Ceph RGW only learned to validate CRC64NVME in **Tentacle 20.2.0** (tracker 70040, fixed via ceph/ceph#61878). The Squid backport of that support is tracked separately at **tracker 70736 and is still not shipped**"

expectations.text: Identifies a bucket index shard exceeding the large-omap key threshold (200000 keys)
expectations.evidence: "one bucket index **shard** has grown past the omap key threshold — `osd_deep_scrub_large_omap_object_key_threshold`, default **200,000** keys."

expectations.text: Recommends radosgw-admin bucket limit check and resharding the bucket (radosgw-admin bucket reshard --num-shards)
expectations.evidence: "radosgw-admin bucket limit check" ... "radosgw-admin bucket reshard --bucket <bucket> --num-shards <n>"

expectations.text: Explains the warning only clears after the next deep scrub of the affected PG (or suggests triggering a deep scrub)
expectations.evidence: "The warning **stays up** until the next deep scrub of the affected PG(s) runs on the normal scrub schedule" and provides "ceph pg deep-scrub <pgid>" to force it sooner.

expectations.text: Explains lifecycle runs only during rgw_lifecycle_work_time (default 00:00-06:00)
expectations.evidence: RGW lifecycle processing only runs during a scheduled work window — `rgw_lifecycle_work_time`, which defaults to **`00:00-06:00`**

expectations.text: Mentions radosgw-admin lc list and/or lc process to inspect or run it now
expectations.evidence: `radosgw-admin lc list` — shows each bucket's LC status ... `radosgw-admin lc process` (optionally `--bucket <name>`) runs the engine immediately

expectations.text: Explains garbage collection delays freeing tail data (rgw_gc_obj_min_wait, 2h) so usage drops later
expectations.evidence: Deleted objects' tail data waits **`rgw_gc_obj_min_wait`** (default **2 hours**) before it becomes eligible for GC.

expectations.text: States CephObjectStoreAccount is experimental
expectations.evidence: RGW accounts via Rook's `CephObjectStoreAccount` CRD (and `accountRef` on `CephObjectStoreUser`) are **experimental in Rook v1.20.7**

expectations.text: States it only works with the Ceph main/CI image (quay.ceph.io/ceph-ci/ceph:main), not with released Ceph like 19.2.6
expectations.evidence: Rook's implementation of it **only works against `quay.ceph.io/ceph-ci/ceph:main`** — a dev/CI image, not a released Ceph build. Your cluster runs Ceph 19.2.6 (a released Squid version), which does not have the support Rook's CRD depends on.

expectations.text: Does not recommend it for production on this stack
expectations.evidence: Treat AWS-style IAM accounts on this Rook/Ceph stack as **not production-ready yet**. ... Don't adopt `CephObjectStoreAccount` on this cluster

expectations.text: Says not to run stale-instances rm in a multisite deployment
expectations.evidence: "No. Do not run `radosgw-admin reshard stale-instances rm` on a multisite cluster."

expectations.text: Cites the Ceph documentation's warning against stale-instance cleanup in multisite
expectations.evidence: "The upstream dynamic-resharding documentation states directly: \"Cleanup of stale instances should not be done in a multisite deployment\" (https://docs.ceph.com/en/squid/radosgw/dynamicresharding/)."

expectations.text: Identifies that Tentacle truncates S3 LastModified timestamps to the second
expectations.evidence: "RGW's `LastModified` timestamp is now truncated to the second**, to match AWS's own S3 semantics. Squid (and earlier) could return `LastModified` with sub-second precision. Tentacle truncates it."

expectations.text: Connects this to sync tools comparing modification times and suggests a mitigation (e.g. compare by size/checksum or a modify-window)
expectations.evidence: "`rclone sync` (and any sync tool that treats mtime/`LastModified` as the primary change-detection signal...) sees a timestamp that doesn't match its prior record and treats the object as changed, triggering a re-upload... prefer checksum-based comparison for this sync pass instead of trusting mtime: `rclone sync --checksum`"

expectations.text: Warns that --bypass-gc can corrupt/delete data of objects created by server-side CopyObject that share tail objects
expectations.evidence: Those copies share tail (rados) objects with the originals rather than duplicating the data. `radosgw-admin bucket rm --purge-objects --bypass-gc` deletes the source objects' tail data immediately instead of routing it through garbage collection ... Skipping it risks **silent corruption of the copied objects that live in your other buckets**

expectations.text: Recommends not using --bypass-gc here (use normal GC deletion)
expectations.evidence: **Drop `--bypass-gc`.** Run `radosgw-admin bucket rm --bucket=big --purge-objects` without it. This queues the deletes through normal GC

expectations.text: Warns that --bypass-gc can corrupt/delete data of objects created by server-side CopyObject that share tail objects
